processing: Moderately fermented ripe pu-erh, blended to an average of about grade 6 according to retailers, with sturdier leaf inside the cake and budded leaf on its surface.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: batches blend tea fermented in earlier years. The 2011 batch 101, for instance, is said to use material fermented in 2009 and 2010.
appearance_dry: A 357 g brown cake with visible budded leaf on the surface and sturdier leaf inside.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as usual for Menghai ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Soft dark brown leaf of mixed size, with some small buds.
taste_profile: Tasting detail varies by batch; expect the typical Menghai ripe profile of earth, dark sweetness and a thick, smooth body.

brewing.notes: Rinse once and use near-boiling water. Break the cake gently so the budded surface does not crumble to dust.

vintage_note: Sold by year and batch in 357 g cakes, seven to a tong. Codes read as year plus batch number, so 1401 is the first batch of 2014 and 1801 the first of 2018; older codes can differ, such as 101 for 2011. First batches are said by retailers to get the best material, though this is trade lore, and leaf grade is not uniform across years.
description:
7262 is one of the Menghai Tea Factory's mainstream ripe cakes, widely sold and often compared with its stablemate 7572. Some retailers go as far as calling it a market benchmark for ripe tea, which is worth reading as trade praise.

Retailers describe a cake built in layers, sturdier leaf inside and budded leaf outside, with moderate fermentation and an average of around grade 6.

Expect a typical Menghai ripe cup, smooth and earthy with a dark sweetness. Use water close to boiling, rinse once, and start with short steeps.

Buy by batch. The code gives the year and run, and specialist shops usually list it. Lots from different years do differ, so a good batch does not guarantee the next one.
history:
The Menghai Tea Factory became fully private in 1996 and adopted the Dayi mark. The exact creation of 7262 is not well documented, though informal readings of factory numbers would place the recipe in 1972, a date that sits awkwardly beside ripe production starting in 1973, so it should not be trusted.

Retailers list Menghai pressings under batch codes for 2011, 2014 and 2018, and a 1998 CNNP-labelled 7262 Yellow Mark cake has also been sold.
